rollout.markets: TP-01-EPCAL in New York metro, with Phoenix – Scottsdale carried in parallel
rollout.rationale: The best MARKET and the best SITE are not the same answer. Phoenix – Scottsdale ranks first on the market screen; New York metro ranks 23 of 23. The pipeline still leads with TP-01-EPCAL because the composite scores the actual dirt — catchment, entitlement posture and infrastructure already in the ground — not the metro average, and on that basis the top two are inside a point of each other. Both go into Tranche 1 diligence and the cost basis decides. A market rank is a prior; a site is evidence.

rollout.markets: Phoenix – Scottsdale, Dallas – Fort Worth, Orlando – Ocala, Houston, Naples – Fort Myers, Las Vegas
rollout.rationale: Tier 1 metros in parallel entitlement once club 1 is permitted and the operating platform exists. Entitlement is the long pole, so it runs concurrently rather than sequentially.

rollout.markets: Under-amenitised existing facilities in proven markets
rollout.rationale: Six metros already have operating clubs. Several are decades old and thin on amenity and residential. Buying and repositioning one compresses a 123-month development cycle to roughly 24 months and is the only route to listing scale inside a fund life.

listing.verdict: NOT LISTABLE BY YEAR 10 ON EITHER ROUTE. 5 stabilised assets are needed. Ground-up reaches that in year 22; even an acquisition-led platform reaches it in year 12. Year 10 is when club 1 finishes ramping, not when a platform lists. The earliest credible route is acquisition-led at year 12; treat a listing as a year-12 stretch outcome, plan the platform for it, and underwrite to a strategic sale or recapitalisation in the meantime.

exits.requires: Delivery and absorption only — no capital-markets event
exits.assessment: HIGHEST CERTAINTY. Returns the majority of invested capital independent of any exit market. This is why the programme is structured as a merchant build.
HIGH CERTAINTY once the club is credible. Collected as the club fills and never repaid.

exits.basis: Permanent debt sized on stabilised NOI
exits.requires: Stabilised operating history and covenant compliance
exits.assessment: PROBABLE. Note the negative-leverage finding: refinancing is a liquidity tool here, not a return enhancer, and should not be sized to the maximum available.

exits.route: Strategic sale of the retained club
exits.requires: A buyer for single-asset special-purpose recreational property
exits.assessment: REALISTIC BUT THIN. Buyer universe is family offices, club operators and member-buyout vehicles, not institutional core capital. Break-even cap is 8.95%; beyond that the club is worth less than it cost to keep.

exits.basis: $113M of club financing capacity plus a $184,849 per-member assessment to reach the exit-cap value
exits.requires: A cohesive, capitalised membership willing to assess itself
exits.assessment: The standard end-state for private clubs, and now priced rather than asserted. PLAUSIBLE BUT NOT A FLOOR. Financing capacity is $113M against a $176M exit-cap value; closing the gap costs each member $184,849, roughly 1.2 initiation fees. Expect a negotiated price below the cap-rate valuation.

exits.basis: Institutional capital into a multi-asset holding company
exits.requires: 4+ assets and a proven operating platform
exits.assessment: PLAUSIBLE IF THE PLATFORM IS BUILT. Requires the second and third clubs, which requires club 1 to prove the model first.

exits.basis: Requires $500M+ equity value and $40M+ recurring NOI
exits.requires: 5 stabilised assets, 2+ years of audited operating history, and a platform management team
exits.assessment: STRETCH OUTCOME, NOT A PLAN. NOT LISTABLE BY YEAR 10 ON EITHER ROUTE. 5 stabilised assets are needed. Ground-up reaches that in year 22; even an acquisition-led platform reaches it in year 12. Year 10 is when club 1 finishes ramping, not when a platform lists. The earliest credible route is acquisition-led at year 12; treat a listing as a year-12 stretch outcome, plan the platform for it, and underwrite to a strategic sale or recapitalisation in the meantime.
